**Summary (partial transcript)**

The team reviewed Q4 firmware release scope for the Vantage line: low-power sleep mode (Tomas), the humidity-drift calibration table patch (Maya), the BLE diagnostic mode (Inès assisting from hardware), and cloud connectivity retry logic (unassigned). After discussing customer impact, the team decided to defer cloud connectivity to the point release after freeze. Tomas explained that units drop the oldest buffered readings after roughly six minutes of outage, the same buffer limit Northfield hit. Exponential backoff mainly reduces server load and battery use, while buffer size is the real data-loss fix. Inès also noted the connectivity code touches the same buffer management as the BLE work. The two will be scoped together in Q1. Tomas reported sleep mode is mostly done: the state machine rewrite is in, and six wake scenarios, including wake during firmware update, are tested. Rev B units show about 40 µA in deep sleep versus about 300 µA today, roughly 7x better. Temperature characterization is blocked on rev C boards. The transcript ends mid-sentence, before the bug backlog, field feedback, rev C status, and action items were covered.

**Action items**

- **Tomas:** Complete current-draw characterization across temperature for sleep mode once rev C boards are available.
- **Tomas / Maya:** Continue sleep mode and calibration patch work for Q4.
- **Inès:** Continue BLE diagnostic mode support.
- **You:** Record the decision to defer cloud connectivity to the post-freeze point release.
- **Team:** Scope cloud connectivity retry and buffer size work together in Q1.

No owners or dates were stated explicitly for these, so they are inferred from the discussion. The transcript is cut off, so later action items may be missing.
